Hi Ethan —

Congrats on getting through procurement. I'm your CS handoff lead for Redwood — I'll coordinate the onboarding plan and the initial infra sizing. To make the kickoff productive, could you confirm the items below before our technical kickoff on 2026-05-27?

Quick checklist (please fill in approximate numbers if exacts are still being gathered):
- Expected daily active users (DAU) or sessions: ____
- Peak concurrent sessions (estimated): ____
- Average tokens per session (user + assistant combined): ____
- Percent of sessions that need long-context (>= 8k tokens): ____
- Required context window for the top 3 flows (chat, summarization, retrieval-augmented QA)
- Any data residency/KMS requirements we should flag for Private mode

Model shortlist: from earlier conversations you indicated interest in a balance of accuracy and cost. Suggested starting shortlist for evaluation on Redwood: 1) Redwood-v2-13B (open-ish baseline), 2) Mistral-7B-Instruct (cost-friendly), 3) 12B-quantized variant for high-throughput gen. If you have other preferences (Claude-style or proprietary models) call them out.

I've attached a blank token-estimates spreadsheet and a one-pager template for implementation constraints. If you can populate the token spreadsheet it's very helpful for our capacity forecasts.

Next steps:
- You fill the quick checklist + token sheet (link/attachment)
- Tech kickoff (2026-05-27) to review flows, SLOs, and canary plan
- Redwood will produce a draft sizing and canary config within 3 business days after kickoff

Thanks — looking forward to getting you running at scale.

Hi Laura —

Thanks — attaching a first-pass token sheet (see attachment) and answers inline below. Alex is our PM for the initiative and will join kickoff.

Checklist (estimates):
- DAU / sessions: ~12k users, 1.5k nightly active sessions
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~300 (US west peak hours)
- Avg tokens per session: 450 tokens (median 310, mean inflated by long sessions)
- Sessions needing long-context (>=8k): ~4% (mostly audit/clinical review flows)
- Context window needs:
  - Chat: 3k typical, 8k for audit flows
  - Summarization (batch): 12k source docs but we can chunk + RAG; prefer 16k context for single-pass
  - RAG QA: usually 2-4k context per query
- Data residency: US-only for PHI; KMS required (AWS KMS), audit logs for 1 year

Model preferences: we'd like to pilot Mistral-7B-Instruct for cheaper paths and Redwood-v2-13B for higher-quality fallbacks. For the long-context summarization flow, we may evaluate a 16k-capable model or a chunked RAG pipeline depending on cost.

I'll be on the kickoff (May 27) and uploaded the completed pulse_token_estimates.xlsx to the Drive folder (link below). Let us know if you want us to generate a sample export of anonymized transcripts for throughput testing.

—Ethan

Team —

I reviewed Ethan's sheet. First impressions and questions for sizing:
- Daily token volume (based on Ethan's numbers): 12k users * 450 tokens ~= 5.4M tokens/day. If peak spikes + nightly batch summarizations included, plan for 7–9M tokens/day buffer.
- Long-context summarization will drive memory usage and KV cache needs. If they want a single-pass 16k model we should account for higher memory per instance and lower batching efficiency.
- Proposed evaluation matrix:
  1) Mistral-7B-Instruct: baseline throughput test, aggressive batching, expect ~750–900 tokens/s per GPU instance (estimate — depends on quantization).
  2) Redwood-v2-13B: quality baseline, lower throughput, plan for sharded 16GB+ GPUs if using 13B float32/16.
  3) 12B-quantized variant: explore 4-bit quantization to increase consolidation and reduce cost; target for high-concurrency routes.

Operational constraints to confirm from PulseHealth: SLOs (p95 latency targets for chat), and retention window for logs. Also confirm whether the 4% long-context users need hard SLO parity with short sessions — if not we can route them to a higher-cost pool with relaxed latency.

I'll draft a preliminary canary plan after the kickoff that includes: model variants per route, initial instance counts, autoscale thresholds, and canary traffic split.

—Monica

Quick technical notes for the draft sizing (I'm pulling numbers from our infra models):
- Baseline assumptions from token sheet: 7.5M tokens/day (conservative).
- If we route short-chat traffic to Mistral-7B-Instruct with batching enabled + prefix cache, we can sustain ~1.2M tokens/hour per dedicated GPU (A100 equivalent) under competitive batching policies. That implies ~6-8 GPUs for baseline daytime load, with autoscale cushion for spikes.
- For long-context summarization (16k), throughput drops significantly — treat these as a separate route pinned to fewer, larger instances. A single 80GB GPU instance (or multi-GPU sharded cluster) can handle ~40–60k tokens/hour depending on model; plan for 1–2 of those for the 4% user class to meet p95 ~1.5s/token.
- KV caching: for chat flows we should enable prefix/KV caching at the route level; this should improve latency and reduce duplicate token work for repeated system prompts and policy text.
- Quantization: testing 4-bit QLoRA-like paths for the 12B-quant variant looks promising — reduces memory to allow more instances per machine and lowers cost per token by ~30–40% in our sims. Need to run fidelity evals during canary.

Action items from my side:
- I'll spin up a CI perf run with sample transcripts Ethan can provide and produce a cost/latency table by 2026-06-02.
- Add canary configs: initial 5% traffic -> 20% over 3 days -> full rollout if quality delta < 1.5 BLEU-equivalent (or agreed metric).

—Dev
